notes.meaning: The Sabbath was the Jewish day of rest, our Saturday. Early on Sunday, as the sky grew light, two women who loved Jesus came to his grave. The other Gospels say they also brought spices to finish preparing his body. This was the third day after his death, just as he had said. Christians have met to worship on this first day ever since.

The earthquake and the angel came before the women arrived. The angel did not raise Jesus. Rolling away the stone showed that heaven had set him free, like a prison door opened because the debt was paid. The stone was moved so the women could go in and see the empty tomb. The angel sitting on it was a sign of victory.
The angel shone like lightning, a picture of God's glory. His snow-white clothes showed purity and joy. Heaven was celebrating that Jesus had risen.
Tough Roman soldiers shook with fear and fainted. Their job was to keep a dead man in his grave, and they could not do it. The rising of Jesus brings joy to his friends but terror to his enemies.

The angel says "you" with force. The guards had reason to fear, but these women did not. They had come looking for Jesus out of love, and heaven saw it. Those who truly seek Jesus have nothing to fear.

Jesus had told them many times that he would rise, and now his word came true. The angel invites them to look at the empty place where his body had lain. The tomb was new, with no other body in it, so there could be no mistake. His body was truly gone because he was truly alive.

The women are given the honor of being the first to carry the good news, even to the apostles. Galilee, in the north, was home for many of his followers. There they could meet him more quietly and safely. "I have told you" is the angel's firm promise that this is true.

They felt fear and great joy at the same time. They were in awe of what they had seen, and the news almost seemed too good to be true. Yet their joy was great, and they ran to share it. People who have met the risen Lord should be eager to tell others.

While the women were obeying, Jesus himself met them. His greeting really means "Rejoice!" They fell at his feet and worshiped him, giving him the honor that belongs to God. God often meets us while we are doing what he asked.
Jesus calms their fear and repeats the angel's message. He calls his disciples "my brothers," even though they had just run away and left him. This tender word showed that he had forgiven them.

At the same moment the guards brought the same news to the chief priests. The women's news filled friends with joy. The guards' news filled enemies with shame. Jesus' enemies were given the clearest proof, yet they still refused to believe.

The leaders met in council and decided to pay the soldiers a lot of money to lie. One sin led them into another as they tried to cover what they had done. People will give freely to a bad cause. Believers should not hold back from supporting a good one.
The story they made up proves itself false. If the guards were asleep, how could they know who took the body? And a few scared, unarmed disciples would not dare take it from armed soldiers.

A Roman soldier could be put to death for sleeping on guard. So the leaders promised to deal with Pilate, the governor, perhaps with another bribe. They could keep the soldiers safe from Pilate, but not from God's justice.

The lie was still being told when Matthew wrote his Gospel. A later Christian writer, Justin Martyr, says it was sent out far and wide. The soldiers had the strongest proof of all, yet money won. Plain evidence alone does not change hearts without the work of the Holy Spirit.

Only eleven disciples were left, because Judas was dead. They obeyed and went to the mountain Jesus had chosen ahead of time. We do not know which mountain it was. Many think this was when he was seen by more than five hundred believers at once.

They worshiped Jesus, but some were unsure at first. Some think the doubters were others in the larger crowd rather than the eleven. Even sincere faith can be weak and wavering. Their slowness to believe also shows they were not easily fooled.

Jesus came close to them, and that cleared away their doubts. As God, all power was always his. Now, as the risen Savior who stands between God and people, the Father has given him all authority in heaven and on earth. This is the ground for the job he is about to give them.

Because Jesus has all authority, they can go without fear. Their task is to make disciples, or followers, from every nation, not just Israel. New disciples are baptized "into the name" of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. It is one name for three persons, the one God Christians call the Trinity. Baptism marks a person as belonging to God.

differ.view: God's promise is to believers and their children, so the children of believers should also be baptized.
Adults are taught first and then baptized, but children of believers are baptized first and taught later, as Jewish boys were circumcised and then taught.
Jesus says to make disciples first and then baptize, so baptism should follow a person's own faith.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars doubt that Jesus spoke these words about Father, Son, and Spirit, thinking them too developed for his time. Others defend them as genuine.

other.label: Orthodox
other.view: The Orthodox Church baptizes by dipping a person three times, once for each name.

notes.meaning: New believers are to be taught to obey everything Jesus commanded. Teachers must pass on his words, not their own ideas. Jesus then promises to be with them every single day by his Spirit, even though his body is in heaven. The promise is for all his people and ministers until the end of the world.
